newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala kidnappers receive death sentence.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala kidnappers receive death sentence.

text.p: For the first time since Guatemala's Congress made kidnapping a capital crime in April, three convicted kidnappers received the death sentence, a prosecutor said on Tuesday.

"Last night they were sentenced to death, which is the punishment set by our laws. The law was applied after the guilt of the accused was shown," state prosecutor Mario Garcia said in a telephone interview on Tuesday.

Carlos Tortola, 20, Cesar Soto, 19, and Marco Fuentes, 20, face death by lethal injection for the October 1995 kidnapping of 76-year-old farmer Adolfo Santizo in the town of Patzicia, 37 miles (60 kilometres) west of Guatemala City, Garcia said.

The kidnappers demanded a $17,000 ransom for Santizo but they were arrested the next day in a nearby hotel where they were holding their victim. A six-day trial concluded on Friday and the judge handed down the sentence late on Monday. The convicted men, none of whom had a criminal record, said they would appeal the sentence.
Hundreds of accused kidnappers are in jail awaiting trial here, and officials anticipate the courts will be handling dozens of death penalty sentences and appeals next year.

Guatemala, like other Latin American countries such as Mexico and Colombia, has suffered a kidnapping epidemic for several years. It peaked this year in April when newspapers were reporting up to three kidnappings a day.
Outraged Guatemalans almost universally support the death sentence for kidnappers and some towns have banners across their main streets proclaiming "Death for Kidnappers."
In September, Guatemala carried out a death sentence for the first time since 1983. Two men convicted of raping and killing a four-year-old girl were executed by firing squad.

Local television stations replayed the gruesome images of the execution, including final pistol shots to the heads of the two men. In reaction to the media coverage, Congress passed a law in October changing the death penalty method to lethal injection.
